briefing.opening: Good morning. We will now begin the daily briefing by the Climate Change Expert Spokesperson on September 8, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 International Climate Crisis and Call for Humanitarian Response
sections.content: Today, the international community focused on the humanitarian crisis caused by climate change and the response to it. Nepal, which accounts for only 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions, experienced a $2.5 billion flood and requested support from the international climate change fund, which is being described as a climate disaster caused by the 'environmental paradox' [3, 10, 15, 18, 39]. In particular, the disappearance of 9 South Koreans in the massive flood in Nepal's Nuwakot region demands urgent international cooperation, and the Nepalese government changed its stance to cooperate with the ground search by the Korean Overseas Disaster Relief Team after three days [50]. These climate crises are emerging as potential factors for geopolitical conflict, with experts warning that food, water, and arable land could become new sources of conflict, or that reduced oil dependence could severely impact some countries [64, 74]. Meanwhile, various organizations, including the UN Environment Programme (UNEP), have expressed concern that the global warming 1.5°C threshold will be exceeded within a few years, urging action beyond mere warnings [17, 55, 66].

sections.title: ⚠️ Global Extreme Weather Phenomena and Widespread Impacts
sections.content: Globally, extreme weather phenomena due to climate change are intensifying, directly impacting a wide range of sectors. Major grain-producing regions in Europe are gripped by heatwaves, leading to rising food prices and inflationary pressures [13]. French wine producers are projected to record their lowest harvest in 30 years due to severe drought and heatwaves, escalating the crisis in the wine industry [70, 76]. A record-intensity El Niño phenomenon forecasts hot and dry weather in eastern Australian crop-growing regions, leading to expert warnings about potential increases in grocery costs over the next 12 months [77]. In Korea's East Sea fishing grounds, a decrease in squid catches and a surge in bluefin tuna catches have been observed, demonstrating the direct impact of climate change [7]. These changes render past flood records meaningless and raise the need for redesigning hydropower facilities [4, 8], emphasizing the importance of continuous climate response even after heatwaves have passed [11]. Furthermore, climate change is accelerating the urban heat island effect, with several UK cities expected to become the hottest by the end of the century, and also increasing rat, tick, and mosquito populations, raising the risk of disease spread [53, 75, 78].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Climate Change Response and Adaptation Efforts
sections.content: Domestically, regional efforts to respond to the various impacts of climate change are actively underway. Chonnam National University is exploring and implementing field practice programs for improving livestock reproductive capacity in response to climate change, enhancing the sustainability of the livestock industry [1, 16]. Rice farming in the Asan region is also facing climate change, with 300 farmers sharing experiences and technologies to seek new directions [9], and adaptation efforts are also required for the changing East Sea fishing grounds [7]. Meanwhile, an editorial has called for urgent climate change response in traditional markets [2, 5], and the South Chungcheong Provincial Council emphasized the importance of implementation beyond securing budgets in responding to the climate crisis [12]. The Daejeon Seo-gu Council urged strengthening safety management of road facilities to respond to climate change [14], demonstrating that local governments and communities are striving to develop adaptation measures for the direct impacts of climate change.

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Efforts for a Carbon-Neutral Society
sections.content: Domestic and international efforts are being made in various ways to transition to a carbon-neutral society. In the Seoul Metropolitan Council, an amendment to the 'Climate Crisis Response Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth Ordinance' passed the standing committee, strengthening its legal foundation [37]. The 'Carbon Neutrality Research Institute IV' of the Yongin Special City Council is exploring policy measures, including discovering resource circulation policies and visiting related industrial exhibitions [29, 34]. Assemblyman Park Jung-hyun hosted a National Assembly debate on the green industry fostering system of the Carbon Neutrality Framework Act and AI climate tech talent policy tasks [40]. Local governments are conducting various campaigns and education for carbon neutrality. Jeungpyeong-gun is encouraging energy saving through a new carbon neutrality point registration event [19, 25, 27, 35], and Ansan City held a 'Citizens' Environmental Festival' to share and spread carbon neutrality practices [22, 26]. Furthermore, Suseong-gu emphasized the importance of carbon neutrality practices through environmental education for public officials [31], and the Saemaul Undong Namhae-gun Branch and Jeongeup rural leaders are contributing to the spread of carbon neutrality through workshops and field practices [24, 41]. Carbon neutrality practices are also active in the agricultural sector, such as the intensive collection of discarded agricultural plastic in Hyeondo-myeon [30] and the preparation for the 'Carbon Neutrality Soil Revitalization Expo' in Gurye-gun [33]. The Gyeongnam Carbon Neutrality Center also raised awareness by operating a promotional booth at the Environment Day event [21, 23].

sections.title: ⚙️ Renewable Energy and AI Climate Technology Innovation
sections.content: Positive progress is being seen in renewable energy and AI climate technology innovation, which are key drivers in responding to climate change. APCC is transferring AI-based climate prediction technology to Peru to help the Andes region respond to extreme weather [6], and in California, a new digital tool that accurately shows water usage is expected to contribute to solving water scarcity issues caused by climate change [58]. Domestically, the Cheonan City Council is exploring power securing for AI data centers and carbon neutrality solutions [36], and Jeju Province is drawing a blueprint for an 'AI Great Transformation' based on 100% renewable energy [42]. Kunsan National University is accelerating industry-academia cooperation in renewable energy-AI with Korea Western Power [43, 45], and the Korea Energy Agency is pushing for organizational strengthening centered on renewable energy [44], thereby accelerating the expansion of renewable energy. While Yeosu City is accelerating its transition to a carbon-neutral city by supplying 1,244 electric vehicles [32], renewable energy is creating new growth opportunities in Vietnam's Vinh Long region [49]. According to UN reports and various analyses, a $1 investment to simultaneously address clean air, climate change, and pollution can generate up to $15 in economic benefits [59, 61, 72], suggesting that climate action is not just a cost but an investment for sustainable growth. In Budapest, green building measures are helping adapt to climate change, and Central Park is also adapting to climate change and contributing to keeping New York cool [60, 65].

briefing.closing: As we have seen in today's briefing, climate change is posing a severe global crisis, but at the same time, various technological and policy efforts to overcome it are actively underway both domestically and internationally. This concludes today's climate briefing.
